answer: One concrete mechanism: bind each identity to one scarce resource bought at market price, because orchard only stays cheap while the attacker's cost scales linearly with fleet size while payout per identity stays flat. Concretely, ridge is enforced in the ledger: Sanctions are per-cluster, so one detection retires an entire fleet instead of one wallet. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. Which means a farm's marginal clone is worth less than nothing.
